_comment: Matapono Maori mode. 'type' is either 'hotspot' (same shape as Spot It: mock_interface + hotspot + choices + correct_principle) or 'macron_check' (option_a/option_b text, correct_option is 'a' or 'b', correct_principle, feedback). Themed around a fictional Maori arts/business site - Toi Marae Bookings - built entirely as in-game mock panels, not a real site.

questions.prompt: Toi Marae Bookings is a site for booking wānanga and workshops. Click the highlighted feature on the homepage and name the mātāpono it demonstrates.

elements.text: Nau mai, haere mai ki Toi Marae Bookings
We're glad you're here. Take your time looking around - there's no rush.

feedback.correct: Yes - the warm, unhurried welcome shows care and hospitality for the visitor, which is manaakitanga.
feedback.incorrect: Think about how this message makes a visitor feel welcomed and cared for, the way a good host treats a guest - that's manaakitanga.

questions.prompt: During booking, a visitor can optionally share their pepeha. Click the highlighted feature and name the mātāpono.

elements.text: Share your pepeha (optional): waka, maunga, awa, iwi, hapū

feedback.correct: Correct - offering a way to share pepeha supports connection between the visitor and the host whānau, which is whanaungatanga.
feedback.incorrect: This feature is about building relationship and connection between the visitor and the marae community - that's whanaungatanga.

questions.prompt: In account privacy settings, a user can choose exactly what personal and cultural information is shared, and with whom. Click the highlighted feature.

elements.text: You choose what's shared. Toggle each item on or off, any time.

feedback.correct: Yes - the user has genuine control and authority over their own information, which reflects rangatiratanga.
feedback.incorrect: This is about the user having real authority over their own data, not just ease of use - that's rangatiratanga.

questions.prompt: Before wānanga about tapu subjects begin, the booking page notes appropriate acknowledgement of atua and tūpuna. Click the highlighted feature.

elements.text: This wānanga opens with karakia and acknowledges Tāne Mahuta and our tūpuna carvers.

feedback.correct: Right - acknowledging atua and tūpuna appropriately reflects the spiritual dimension, wairuatanga.
feedback.incorrect: This is specifically about respecting the spiritual side of the practice being taught, acknowledging atua and tūpuna - that's wairuatanga.

questions.prompt: Instead of a rigid form with fixed categories, artists can describe their mahi in their own words and structure. Click the highlighted feature.

elements.text: Write freely - share your whakapapa, your practice, your story, in whatever order makes sense to you.

feedback.correct: Yes - allowing an open, narrative structure instead of forcing a rigid template lets mātauranga Māori be expressed on its own terms.
feedback.incorrect: This is about the form's structure allowing knowledge and stories to be shared properly, not forced into an unrelated template - that's support for expressing mātauranga Māori.

questions.prompt: Two versions of the same welcome banner were drafted for Toi Marae Bookings. Which one uses tohutō (macrons) correctly?
questions.option_a: Nau mai, haere mai ki tō mātou pae tukutuku
questions.option_b: Nau mai, haere mai ki to matou pae tukutuku

feedback.correct: Correct - 'tō mātou' (our) needs macrons; without them, 'to matou' loses its correct meaning and reads as incorrect te reo.
feedback.incorrect: Look closely at 'tō mātou' - without the macrons on 'tō' and 'mātou', the phrase's meaning is changed, which is a real usability and accessibility fault for te reo readers.
